newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grade barrels find favor, EFP's continue firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grade barrels find favor, EFP's continue firm.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices found a comfortable trading zone Tuesday afternoon, maintaining domestic grade barrel advances staked out from Monday.

Traders said both sweet and sour barrels benefitted from a slew of fundamental factors, notably the lack of foreign crudes available in the Gulf and expectations for maintenance-related production cuts for North Sea barrels in June. In general, traders said foreign offerings for second-half June were seen slacking off.
"We've been hearing West African is coming, some Brent, but we haven't seen much of anything," said a cash crude trader.
Outright June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing prices were a touch lower, declining five cents to $21.30-40 a barrel.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was steady from morning deals at June WTI/Cushing +13 cents, with Midland/WTI also steady around a 30-31 cents discount to the benchmark.
West Texas Sour/Midland firmed as well, trading hands at WTI/Cushing -$1.38, and currently talked at minus $1.40-35.
June WTI/Cushing Postings fluctuated with the shrinking June/July roll of plus four cents. Postings found favor around $2.10-15, traders said.
Exchange for physicals stayed strong at plus 10-12 cents, attracting increased attention on expectations for more foreign crude deliveries against NYMEX paper positions for June.

Fundamental concerns over production threats cropped into the market, led by Shell announcing it shut 120,000 barrels per day of Nigerian production over the weekend. Continued communal unrest forced closure of five flow stations.
